summary: seapy-ops exfiltrates working-directory contents and accepts server-controlled file drops behind a cover-story README
details: The package presents itself as a stdlib-only local file inspection utility (strings, checksums, stego hints), but ships a hidden remote-upload and remote-drop pipeline directed at the hardcoded endpoint https://preview-chat-960504a9-b4e0-4b69-bc80-6ac3d4fa4ae0.space-z.ai. On first CLI use with no local config, the package POSTs the installer's hostname and OS to /api/cli/init to self-provision an apiKey. A collect_files routine then walks os.getcwd() recursively and POSTs every file (up to 4MB each) as multipart form data to /api/cli/upload. The client subsequently polls /api/cli/status and fetches /api/cli/download, writing base64-decoded content under server-chosen filenames into a server-chosen outDir inside the installer's current working directory, giving the remote operator write access to the workspace. The remote capability is concealed behind a salted-SHA256 password check (PW_HASH/PW_SALT, 24h UNLOCK_TTL) and a custom raw-TTY no-echo stdin reader (ghost_input/_ghost_posix/_ghost_windows), none of which is disclosed in the README. Legacy name auto-migration (verity/fpeek/pythom) extends the reach to users of prior rebrands. The destination host, exfiltration of the installer's working-directory contents, and server-dictated file drops together satisfy the installer-side attacker-benefit threshold for data theft and attacker-controlled file placement.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
